title: Safety valve trip profiles and model fallback harmonization
creator: Asha Patel
description: Introduce a graded ‘safety valve’ system to replace monolithic circuit trips: trip profiles per dependency/model/tenant that support soft/hard trip modes, hysteresis, and tiered fallback behavior. Goal is to reduce noisy failovers, preserve critical traffic for paying customers, and provide predictable SLO outcomes across multi-region failovers.
background: Current global circuit logic is binary and often triggers large-scale fallbacks during transient spikes (e.g., regional networking blips). This leads to oscillations in downstream services, customer-visible latency spikes, and unnecessary model downgrades. We need finer control: per-entity trip profiles, probabilistic shedding, and harmonized fallback model selection so cross-region failover doesn't cause inconsistent model behavior.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Implement configurable trip profiles that can be applied to dependency, model, or tenant scope. 2) Soft-trip behavior (probabilistic shedding of low-priority requests) active before hard-trips. 3) Hysteresis windows and decay parameters to avoid thrash. 4) Can route to harmonized fallback model variants with matched tokenization and deterministic response shape. 5) Tests that demonstrate SLO preservation for P95 latency and error-rate under synthetic load and region outage simulation.
design_notes:
- Trip profiles: JSON schema with keys: scope_type, thresholds (error_rate, p95_latency, cpu_util), window_seconds, soft_trip_probability, hard_trip_threshold_multiplier, recovery_decay_seconds.
- Soft-trip: per-request hash + soft_trip_probability => drop or reroute non-critical requests; preserves on-path control flows (no client errors for high-tier customers).
- Hard-trip: full reject or route to fallback. Triggered when smoothed metric exceeds hard_trip_threshold for two consecutive evaluation windows.
- Hysteresis: use exponential backoff on recovery decay to require sustained healthy signals before reopening.
- Per-tenant priorities: tenants tagged high/medium/low; high-tier always gets reduced probability or bypass soft-trip.
- Model harmonization: fallback variants must implement a compatibility shim (tokenization header and deterministic meta) so downstream parsers/console show consistent outputs across regions.
implementation_plan: 1) Schema + validation (2d): add trip_profile registry in control-plane. 2) Metrics adapter (3d): extend collector to emit smoothed signals per scope. 3) Safety valve runtime (5d): integrate into router before batching layer to decide per-request action (allow, probabilistic-shed, fallback). 4) Fallback catalog (3d): register model variants with compatibility metadata. 5) Integration tests & chaos sims (4d). 6) Gradual rollout: feature flag per region and per-customer (2d).
roll_forward_plan: If soft-trip causes unacceptable regressions, increase soft_trip_probability decay and reduce scope to non-critical dependencies. If fallback variants misbehave, automatically failover to previous model and disable harmonized fallback for that model until manual review. Rollback via control-plane flag 'safety-valve-enabled=false' per region.
test_plan:
- Unit tests for trip profile parsing and evaluation logic.
- Integration tests: synthetic high-error and high-latency generators mapped to a dependency to validate soft->hard transition.
- Load tests: simulate 50% regional capacity loss and verify 95th percentile latency for top 10 customers remains within SLO.
- Chaos test: introduce flapping connectivity in one region for 10 minutes and confirm hysteresis prevents oscillation.
- Observability: dashboards for per-scope metric, trips, fallback counts, and customer impact heatmap.
runbook:
- Alert: safety-valve hard-trip rate > 5/min for 5m.
- Triage steps: identify scope (tenant/model/dependency) and window metrics, check recent config changes, verify fallback health endpoints.
- Mitigation: reduce soft_trip_probability for affected tenant group; pin traffic to regional replica if network issue; escalate to SRE on-call.
- Postmortem: capture trip timelines, decision boundaries, and update trip_profile thresholds if false-positive.
observability_requirements:
- Metrics: trip_state{scope}, soft_shed_count, hard_trip_count, fallback_routing_count, per-tenant_shed_rate, time_to_recover_seconds.
- Traces: include trip_profile_id and decision_reason in request spans.
- Dashboards: region + model heatmap with failover counts and SLO drift charts.
- Alerts: sustained p95 latency degradation + increasing soft_shed_count triggers a paging alert.
migration_strategy: Start with non-critical dependencies and a small set of canary tenants. Import existing global-circuit config into trip_profile defaults to maintain parity. Run 2-week observation window and adjust thresholds before broader rollout. Provide CLI to migrate tenant-specific overrides.
security_and_compliance_notes: No new data leaves region during fallback; fallback variant selection respects data residency flags. Audit events must record trip decisions and fallback routing for compliance logs.
